A.text: The VLAN must exist and have at least one active Layer 2 port
A.rationale: An SVI normally depends on the VLAN being active on the switch.

B.text: The SVI must be configured as a physical trunk port
B.rationale: An SVI is a logical interface, not a physical trunk port.

C.text: The switch must become the root bridge for that VLAN
C.rationale: Being root bridge is not required for an SVI to be operational.

D.text: A default route must be learned through OSPF
D.rationale: The SVI state does not depend on learning a default route.

113.scenario: A trunk currently allows VLANs 10, 20, and 30. The administrator enters switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40.
113.explanation: The add keyword adds VLAN 40 to the existing list without replacing the VLANs already permitted. The list becomes 10, 20, 30, and 40.

A.rationale: The add keyword preserves the existing list and adds the new VLAN.

B.rationale: That result would match a command without the add keyword.

C.text: VLAN 40 automatically becomes the native VLAN
C.rationale: The allowed VLAN list does not change the native VLAN.

D.text: The port automatically becomes a VLAN 40 access port
D.rationale: The command does not change the port from trunk mode.

114.question_text: What is the effect of configuring no lldp transmit on an interface while leaving LLDP globally enabled?
114.explanation: The interface stops sending LLDP advertisements but can still receive them if reception is not disabled. Transmit and receive directions can be configured separately.

A.text: The interface no longer sends LLDP advertisements but can still receive them
A.rationale: The command disables only the transmit direction.

B.text: LLDP is disabled globally on the entire switch
B.rationale: An interface command does not disable LLDP on all ports.

C.text: The interface sends LLDP but ignores received advertisements
C.rationale: This would correspond to disabling receive, not transmit.

D.text: Cisco Discovery Protocol is automatically disabled
D.rationale: LLDP and Cisco Discovery Protocol are configured independently.

115.scenario: Two interfaces intended for the same EtherChannel have the same speed, but one is configured as an access port and the other as a trunk.
115.question_text: Why is the LACP bundle likely to fail?
115.explanation: Layer 2 EtherChannel member interfaces must have compatible switching parameters, including access or trunk mode and VLAN settings. A mismatch prevents a stable logical channel from forming.

A.text: The members have inconsistent Layer 2 parameters
A.rationale: LACP does not properly bundle incompatible access and trunk ports.

B.text: LACP always requires four physical links
B.rationale: An EtherChannel can form with fewer than four links.

C.text: The interfaces must have identical IPv6 link-local addresses
C.rationale: A Layer 2 EtherChannel does not depend on such IPv6 addresses.

D.text: Each member must use a different native VLAN
D.rationale: VLAN parameters must be consistent, not different.

116.scenario: SW1 has two paths to the root bridge. The first has a total cost of 19 and the second has a total cost of 38.
116.question_text: Which path does SW1 normally choose for its root port?
116.explanation: The root port is selected according to the superior BPDU, including the lowest total cost to the root bridge. Therefore, the path with cost 19 is preferred.

A.rationale: STP prefers the lowest cost to the root bridge.

B.rationale: A higher cost is less favorable during root port selection.

C.text: Both paths simultaneously become root ports
C.rationale: A nonroot switch normally has one root port per instance.

D.text: Neither path, because the cost must equal zero
D.rationale: Only the root bridge initially advertises a root path cost of zero.

117.question_text: On which type of port should PortFast normally be enabled?
117.explanation: PortFast is intended for edge ports connected to a single endpoint because it allows rapid transition to forwarding. It should not be used carelessly on a link that could create a switching loop.

A.text: An access port connected to an end-user host
A.rationale: An endpoint should not participate in the STP topology and benefits from immediate convergence.

B.text: A redundant trunk between two switches
B.rationale: An interswitch trunk should normally participate fully in STP.

C.text: The root port of a distribution switch
C.rationale: The root port is part of the redundant topology and should not be treated as an edge port.

D.text: An EtherChannel link between two core switches
D.rationale: A core-to-core link can carry potential loops and requires normal STP behavior.

118.scenario: A nondesignated port normally receives BPDUs. Because of a unidirectional failure, those BPDUs stop arriving while the link remains physically up.
118.question_text: Which feature prevents this port from incorrectly transitioning to forwarding?
118.explanation: Loop guard places the port into a loop-inconsistent state when expected BPDUs disappear. It therefore protects against certain loops caused by unidirectional failures.

A.rationale: Loop guard blocks the port when expected BPDUs are no longer received.

B.rationale: Root guard reacts to superior BPDUs that threaten the expected root location.

C.rationale: BPDU guard primarily protects PortFast ports that receive an unexpected BPDU.

D.rationale: BPDU filter suppresses BPDUs and could hide the problem rather than detect it.

119.scenario: A wireless LAN controller uses multiple physical interfaces bundled to increase capacity and resilience toward the switch.
119.question_text: How is the resulting logical connection generally presented to the switch?
119.explanation: A controller LAG bundles multiple physical links into one logical interface. The switch generally configures an EtherChannel and carries multiple VLANs over an 802.1Q trunk.

A.text: As a trunk EtherChannel carrying multiple VLANs
A.rationale: The LAG combines link capacity and the trunk carries WLAN VLANs.

B.text: As multiple independent access ports in the same VLAN
B.rationale: This does not correctly represent a logical multi-VLAN LAG.

C.rationale: The console is for local management, not WLAN traffic transport.

D.text: As a mandatory GRE tunnel over each cable
D.rationale: The physical bundle toward the switch relies on EtherChannel, not a GRE tunnel per cable.

120.scenario: An enterprise WLAN must use WPA2 with one preshared key shared by clients.
120.question_text: Which parameter combination meets this requirement in the controller GUI?
120.explanation: WPA2 with PSK generally uses AES encryption and a preshared key configured on the WLAN and clients. 802.1X mode would use an authentication server instead of a shared key.

A.rationale: This combination matches a WPA2 Personal WLAN with a shared key.

B.rationale: 802.1X normally requires an authentication service such as RADIUS.

C.rationale: WEP is a weak legacy protocol and does not meet the WPA2 requirement.

D.text: No encryption and a hidden SSID
D.rationale: Hiding the SSID does not replace WPA2 encryption.

121.question_text: In a Cisco IOS routing table, what does a route marked with code L represent?
121.explanation: A local route exactly matches the IP address configured on a router interface. In IPv4, it generally appears with a /32 prefix.

A.rationale: Code L identifies a local route to the interface address.

B.rationale: LACP bundles links and does not learn routes.

C.rationale: A static route uses code S.

D.rationale: LLDP discovers Layer 2 neighbors and does not create routes.

122.scenario: The table contains two static routes to 10.50.0.0/16, each with the same administrative distance and cost but with different next hops.
122.question_text: What behavior is expected if both next hops are reachable?
122.explanation: Routes with the same prefix, source, and metric can be installed as equal-cost paths. The router can then distribute flows according to its load-balancing mechanism.

A.text: Both paths can be installed for load balancing
A.rationale: The routes are equivalent according to the selection criteria.

B.text: The first-entered route is always the only one installed
B.rationale: Entry order does not force exclusion of an equal-cost path.

C.text: The route with the numerically highest next hop always wins
C.rationale: The numerical value of the next hop is not the preference criterion.

D.text: No route is installed because the prefix is duplicated
D.rationale: Equal-cost paths to the same prefix can coexist.

123.question_text: Which static route is considered fully specified?
123.explanation: A fully specified static route includes both the exit interface and the next-hop address. This form can be useful on a multiaccess network to avoid certain resolution ambiguities.

A.text: A route specifying both the exit interface and next hop
A.rationale: These two pieces of information make the route fully specified.

B.text: A route specifying only the destination network
B.rationale: A static route must also indicate how to reach the destination.

C.text: A route learned automatically through OSPF
C.rationale: An OSPF route is not a static route.

D.text: A route with no mask or prefix
D.rationale: The destination network must be defined.

124.question_text: What information must normally accompany an IPv6 link-local address used as the next hop in a static route?
124.explanation: A link-local address is unique only on its link. The exit interface must therefore be specified to identify the link on which the next hop is reachable.

A.rationale: The interface determines the scope of the link-local next hop.

B.rationale: DNS does not identify the scope of the link-local address in the command.

C.rationale: The Bridge ID belongs to STP and is not used in an IPv6 route.

D.rationale: WLAN settings do not define a static route next hop.

125.scenario: An OSPF route to 172.20.0.0/16 is active. A static route to the same prefix is configured with an administrative distance of 200.
125.question_text: Why does the static route not appear as the primary path?
125.explanation: OSPF has an administrative distance lower than 200. The floating static route therefore remains a backup and becomes active only if the OSPF route disappears.

A.text: Its administrative distance is higher than the OSPF route's
A.rationale: The route from the more trusted source is preferred for the same prefix.

B.text: Its prefix is longer than the OSPF route's
B.rationale: Both routes target the same prefix in the scenario.

C.text: OSPF forbids all backup static routes
C.rationale: A floating static route is specifically designed to back up a dynamic protocol.

D.text: A static route must always have an administrative distance of zero
D.rationale: A static route's administrative distance can be configured and need not be zero.

126.question_text: Two directly connected OSPFv2 routers use the same subnet, but one configures area 0 and the other area 10. What result is expected?
126.explanation: OSPF neighbors must advertise the same area ID on the link. An area mismatch prevents adjacency formation.

A.rationale: The area ID must match between neighbors.

B.rationale: OSPF does not automatically negotiate a common area.

C.rationale: BDR election does not resolve an area mismatch.

D.text: A static route is created between the areas
D.rationale: OSPF does not automatically create a static route to fix the configuration.

127.question_text: What is the effect of a Hello or Dead interval mismatch between two OSPFv2 neighbors on the same link?
127.explanation: Hello and Dead intervals are among the parameters that must match. A mismatch generally prevents the routers from becoming fully adjacent neighbors.

A.text: The adjacency does not form correctly
A.rationale: Incompatible timers are detected in Hello packets.

B.text: The routers automatically use the average of the two values
B.rationale: OSPF does not negotiate an average for these intervals.

C.text: The router with the shortest interval always becomes DR
C.rationale: Timers do not directly determine DR election.

D.rationale: NTP synchronizes time, not OSPF parameters.

128.scenario: Network 10.10.40.0/24 must be advertised by OSPF, but no OSPF neighbor should form on the user-facing interface.
128.question_text: Which configuration best meets this requirement?
128.explanation: passive-interface prevents Hello packets from being sent on the interface while allowing the connected network to be advertised by OSPF. The interface continues carrying normal IP traffic.

A.text: Configure the interface as passive in OSPF
A.rationale: The network remains advertised without neighbor formation on that LAN.

B.rationale: This would also remove user connectivity.

C.text: Remove the IP address from the interface
C.rationale: Without an address, the connected network can no longer be advertised normally.

D.rationale: Priority affects DR election, not Hello transmission.

129.question_text: On an OSPF link configured as point-to-point, which statement is correct?
129.explanation: An OSPF point-to-point network does not perform a DR or BDR election. The two routers can directly form a full adjacency.

A.text: No DR or BDR election occurs
A.rationale: The point-to-point type does not require a designated router.

B.text: A DR and BDR are always elected
B.rationale: This election primarily belongs to broadcast and NBMA networks.

C.text: The routers always remain in the 2-WAY state
C.rationale: The two point-to-point neighbors normally form a FULL adjacency.

D.text: OSPF uses only static routes on this link
D.rationale: The network type does not turn OSPF into static routing.

130.scenario: Two routers reach EXSTART, then the adjacency repeatedly resets. Areas and timers match.
130.question_text: Which mismatch is a classic cause of this symptom?
130.explanation: An MTU mismatch can prevent proper exchange of Database Description packets and stall the adjacency around EXSTART or EXCHANGE.

A.rationale: Incompatible MTUs can interrupt OSPF database negotiation.

B.rationale: The SSID belongs to WLANs and does not affect a wired OSPF adjacency.

C.rationale: OSPF neighbors do not need to use the same NTP server.

D.text: A different voice VLAN on a phone
D.rationale: That setting does not directly explain an OSPF EXSTART failure.

131.question_text: A new OSPF router with a higher priority joins a broadcast network where a DR and BDR are already elected. What normally happens?
131.explanation: DR and BDR election is nonpreemptive. Therefore, the new router does not immediately replace the existing DR simply because it has a higher priority.

A.text: The existing DR keeps its role until a new election
A.rationale: OSPF does not preempt an already elected DR.

B.text: The new router immediately becomes DR
B.rationale: A higher priority does not trigger automatic preemption.

C.text: All neighbors permanently return to INIT state
C.rationale: The arrival of a router does not force this permanent behavior.

D.text: The BDR automatically becomes the STP root bridge
D.rationale: OSPF and STP roles are independent.

132.question_text: After manually changing the router ID of an active OSPF process, which action is generally required for the new value to be used?
132.explanation: The router ID is selected when the process starts. Therefore, the OSPF process must be restarted or cleared to apply the new identifier.

A.text: Restart or clear the OSPF process
A.rationale: Router ID selection is not immediately recalculated while the process runs.

B.rationale: DHCP does not control the OSPF router ID.

C.text: Wait for MAC address table aging
C.rationale: MAC aging is independent of OSPF.

D.rationale: The native VLAN does not apply a router ID change.

133.scenario: R1 was the HSRP active router. After a failure, R2 becomes active. R1 returns with a higher priority but does not retake the role.
133.question_text: Which feature must be configured on R1 so it can automatically retake the active role?
133.explanation: Preemption allows a higher-priority HSRP router to retake the active role when it becomes available again. Without preemption, the currently active router generally keeps its role.

A.rationale: Preemption permits active-role takeover based on priority.

B.rationale: PortFast concerns STP convergence on edge ports.

C.rationale: DHCP snooping protects Layer 2 DHCP exchanges.

D.rationale: NAT overload translates multiple addresses and does not control HSRP.

134.scenario: A NAT pool contains ten global addresses, and the configuration does not use overload. Ten dynamic translations are already active.
134.question_text: What happens when an eleventh inside host attempts to create a new translation?
134.explanation: Without overload, each dynamic translation consumes a distinct global address from the pool. When the pool is exhausted, no new translation can be created until an entry is released.

A.text: The new translation fails until a pool address becomes available
A.rationale: The pool has no unused global address remaining.

B.text: The router automatically uses PAT even without overload
B.rationale: PAT must be explicitly configured with overload.

C.text: The router assigns a link-local address to the new host
C.rationale: NAT does not perform DHCP assignment for the client.

D.text: The router converts the translation into an OSPF route
D.rationale: NAT and OSPF perform independent functions.

135.question_text: In the NTP hierarchy, what does a lower stratum number indicate?
135.explanation: A lower stratum indicates a source closer to a reference clock. Servers synchronized to that source generally advertise a stratum one level higher.

A.text: The source is closer to the reference clock
A.rationale: Stratum measures logical distance from the time reference.

B.rationale: Stratum does not measure link capacity.

C.text: The source uses a longer IP prefix
C.rationale: Stratum is independent of IP prefix length.

D.text: The source sends BPDUs more frequently
D.rationale: BPDUs belong to STP, not NTP.

136.question_text: Which DNS record type directly maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
136.explanation: An AAAA record contains an IPv6 address. An A record contains an IPv4 address, while a CNAME creates an alias.

A.rationale: AAAA is the record type used for an IPv6 address.

B.rationale: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address.

C.rationale: MX identifies a domain's mail servers.

D.rationale: PTR is primarily used for reverse lookup.

137.question_text: Which SNMP function allows an agent to spontaneously send a notification to the manager without waiting for a poll?
137.explanation: An SNMP trap is an unsolicited notification sent by the agent. GET polling is initiated by the manager and occurs at a defined interval.

A.rationale: A trap reports an event without a prior manager request.

B.rationale: GET is initiated by the manager, not spontaneously by the agent.

C.rationale: DNS does not carry SNMP events.

D.rationale: A Hello discovers OSPF neighbors and does not notify an SNMP manager.

138.question_text: Which statement correctly compares TFTP and FTP?
138.explanation: TFTP uses UDP and provides a simple transfer mechanism without traditional built-in user authentication. FTP uses TCP and offers more features, including an authenticated session.

A.text: TFTP uses UDP, while FTP uses TCP and can authenticate the user
A.rationale: This distinction matches the general capabilities of the two protocols.

B.text: TFTP always encrypts files, unlike FTP
B.rationale: TFTP provides no native encryption, and classic FTP is also unencrypted.

C.text: FTP operates only through Layer 2 broadcast
C.rationale: FTP uses routable TCP connections.

D.rationale: TFTP does not provide this built-in authentication.

139.scenario: A critical vulnerability is discovered on a server. No patch is available yet, but access to the service can be limited to a few management addresses.
139.question_text: Which action is the best temporary mitigation?
139.explanation: An ACL limiting access reduces exposure to the vulnerability until a patch is installed. It does not remove the vulnerability but lowers the likelihood of exploitation.

A.text: Limit access to the service with a restrictive ACL
A.rationale: This measure immediately reduces the exposed attack surface.

B.text: Publish the server address to simplify testing
B.rationale: This would increase exposure to the threat.

C.rationale: Removing logs reduces visibility without mitigating the vulnerability.

D.text: Reuse the same password on every server
D.rationale: This practice increases the risk of broad compromise.

140.scenario: Unauthorized people regularly follow employees through a secured door before it closes.
140.question_text: Which measure most directly addresses this tailgating risk?
140.explanation: A mantrap controlling passage of one person at a time reduces tailgating. Employee awareness can complement this physical control.

A.text: Install a mantrap limiting passage to one person
A.rationale: The mantrap physically prevents multiple people from using one authentication.

B.rationale: Address planning does not control physical building access.

C.rationale: LACP bundles network links and is not a physical control.

D.text: Change the native VLAN every week
D.rationale: This does not prevent a person from entering through a secured door.

141.question_text: Why is enable secret preferred over enable password on Cisco IOS?
141.explanation: enable secret protects the privileged-mode secret with a stronger hashing mechanism than the historical storage of enable password. When both are configured, enable secret is used.

A.text: It better protects the privileged-mode secret
A.rationale: enable secret is designed for safer secret storage.

B.text: It automatically enables SSH with no other configuration
B.rationale: SSH also requires keys and suitable VTY configuration.

C.text: It encrypts all traffic transiting the router
C.rationale: The command protects a local secret, not user packets.

D.rationale: The privileged secret and ACL filtering are separate functions.

142.question_text: Which combination constitutes true multifactor authentication?
142.explanation: Multifactor authentication combines factors from different categories, such as something the user knows and something the user has. Two memorized secrets remain one factor type.

A.text: A password and a code generated by an app on the phone
A.rationale: This combination joins knowledge and possession.

B.text: A password and a security question
B.rationale: Both items are knowledge factors.

C.rationale: Two memorized secrets do not create two factor categories.

D.rationale: The username identifies the account but is not a separate secret factor.

143.question_text: Which statement correctly describes IPsec tunnel mode?
143.explanation: Tunnel mode protects the original IP packet and adds a new outer IP header. It is commonly used between gateways in a site-to-site VPN.

A.text: It encapsulates the original IP packet with a new outer IP header
A.rationale: This full encapsulation characterizes tunnel mode.

B.text: It encrypts only the Ethernet MAC address field
B.rationale: IPsec protects data at the IP layer, not only the MAC field.

C.text: It replaces encryption with a simple ACL
C.rationale: An ACL may select traffic but does not provide IPsec encryption.

D.text: It requires both hosts to use the same IP address
D.rationale: IPsec peers use distinct routable addresses.

144.question_text: What happens when a packet matches no entry in an IPv4 ACL?
144.explanation: An implicit deny any statement exists at the end of every ACL. Therefore, the packet is dropped if no earlier entry permitted it.

A.text: The packet is dropped by the implicit deny any
A.rationale: No match results in the final implicit deny.

B.text: The packet is permitted by default
B.rationale: An ACL does not use an implicit permit any.

C.text: The packet is sent to the DHCP server
C.rationale: ACL processing does not automatically redirect packets to DHCP.

D.text: The packet is converted into a multicast frame
D.rationale: An ACL filters traffic and does not change its destination type.

145.scenario: The legitimate DHCP server is reachable through uplink port Gi1/0/48. All other ports connect users.
145.question_text: Which port should normally be configured as trusted for DHCP snooping?
145.explanation: The port leading to the legitimate DHCP server should be trusted to allow server messages such as DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK. User ports remain untrusted to block rogue DHCP servers.

A.text: Gi1/0/48, the port leading to the legitimate DHCP server
A.rationale: Authorized DHCP replies must enter through a trusted port.

B.rationale: User ports should normally remain untrusted.

C.rationale: The console port does not carry client DHCP exchanges.

D.text: No port, because trusted blocks DHCP replies
D.rationale: A trusted port permits server messages; it does not block them.

146.scenario: An enterprise must apply the same policy to 300 switches and reduce configuration differences among devices.
146.question_text: Which advantage of a controller-based architecture best meets this need?
146.explanation: A controller provides a central point to define and deploy consistent policy across many devices. This reduces repetitive manual changes and configuration drift.

A.rationale: Central policy improves consistency at scale.

B.rationale: The controller does not remove the physical infrastructure.

C.text: The requirement to configure every port only by console
C.rationale: That method would increase manual work rather than reduce it.

D.rationale: TCP and STP perform different functions and are not interchangeable.

147.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the underlay and overlay?
147.explanation: The underlay provides foundational IP connectivity between devices. The overlay builds a virtual topology above it and depends on the reachability provided by the underlay.

A.text: The underlay transports the overlay, which provides virtual connectivity
A.rationale: The overlay depends on the underlying transport network.

B.text: The overlay replaces all physical cables
B.rationale: A virtual topology still requires transport infrastructure.

C.text: The underlay is only a JSON file
C.rationale: The underlay is the transport network, not a data format.

D.text: The overlay is the controller's DHCP server
D.rationale: DHCP can provide IP parameters but does not define the overlay.

148.scenario: A generative AI assistant proposes a configuration to fix a critical network incident.
148.question_text: Which action is most appropriate before applying the configuration in production?
148.explanation: Generative AI output can contain errors or recommendations that do not fit the context. The engineer must validate the proposal, its assumptions, and its impact before deployment.

A.text: Validate the configuration and its impact in the real context
A.rationale: Human oversight reduces the risk of applying an incorrect response.

B.text: Apply it immediately because the AI uses a trained model
B.rationale: A trained model can still produce an incorrect answer.

C.text: Disable all logs before the change
C.rationale: Logs are useful for verifying the result and diagnosing failure.

D.text: Delete the backup of the current configuration
D.rationale: A backup supports rollback if the change fails.

149.question_text: Which REST API characteristic means that each request must contain the information required for processing without depending on session state stored by the server?
149.explanation: The stateless principle requires each request to be self-contained. The server may retain resources, but it does not depend on client session context between requests.

A.rationale: Each request carries the context required for processing.

B.rationale: This term does not describe a REST characteristic.

C.rationale: MAC aging belongs to Ethernet switching.

D.rationale: Route summarization does not define API session handling.

150.question_text: In the JSON document {"devices":["R1","R2"],"count":2}, which element is an array?
150.explanation: Square brackets delimit a JSON array. Therefore, the value of devices is an array of two strings, while count contains a number.

A.rationale: Square brackets identify the ordered array collection.

B.rationale: devices is a key in the JSON object, not the array itself.

C.rationale: 2 is a JSON numeric value.

D.rationale: This is a key-value pair, not an array.

151.question_text: Match each protocol to its OSI model layer.
151.explanation: HTTP is an application protocol (L7). TCP provides reliable transport (L4). IP handles inter-network routing (L3). Ethernet defines frame format and MAC addressing (L2).

152.question_text: Match each TCP port number to its standard service.
152.explanation: Ports 0-1023 are IANA-assigned "well-known ports". SSH=22 (encrypted), Telnet=23 (unencrypted), DNS=53, HTTP=80, HTTPS=443.

153.question_text: Match each route source to its default Cisco administrative distance.
153.explanation: Administrative distance (AD) expresses the preference between route sources. Cisco defaults: connected=0, static=1, eBGP=20, EIGRP internal=90, OSPF=110, RIP=120, iBGP=200.

154.question_text: Match each IPv6 address type to its prefix.
154.explanation: RFC 4291: global unicast=2000::/3, link-local=FE80::/10, unique local=FC00::/7, multicast=FF00::/8, loopback=::1/128.

155.question_text: Match each NAT type to its behavior.
155.explanation: Static NAT: fixed 1:1 mapping (often for exposed internal servers). Dynamic NAT: mapping from a pool of public addresses. PAT (NAT overload): many private addresses share ONE public address by differentiating sessions with source ports.

156.question_text: Match each Wi-Fi standard to its frequency band(s).
156.explanation: 802.11a: 5 GHz only. 802.11b: 2.4 GHz only. 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4): dual-band 2.4 and 5 GHz. 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5): 5 GHz only. 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6): dual-band 2.4 and 5 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E adds the 6 GHz band).

157.question_text: Match each STP (802.1D) port state to its behavior.
157.explanation: Classic STP sequence: Blocking → Listening → Learning → Forwarding (Disabled = admin down). The port only learns MACs and forwards traffic in the matching final states.

158.question_text: Match each cable type to its typical use.
158.explanation: Straight-through connects two devices of different types (PC-switch). Crossover connects two devices of the same type (switch-switch), useful before auto-MDIX. Rollover (Cisco blue console cable) is used to access the CLI via the console port. Single-mode fiber: long distances.

159.question_text: Select TWO primary functions of a router.
159.explanation: A router forwards packets between different IP networks based on a routing table built from dynamic protocols and static routes.

A.text: Route packets between different IP networks
A.rationale: Core role of a router (Layer 3).

B.rationale: Foundation of forwarding decisions.

C.text: Learn the MAC addresses of LAN hosts
C.rationale: That is the role of a switch (Layer 2), not a router.

D.text: Switch Ethernet frames within a VLAN
D.rationale: A switching function (Layer 2), not routing.

E.text: Dynamically assign IP addresses via DHCP
E.rationale: Optional via ip helper-address or integrated DHCP role, not a primary function.

160.question_text: Select TWO characteristics of a Layer 2 switch.
160.explanation: A Layer 2 switch makes forwarding decisions based on destination MAC addresses and creates one collision domain per port through switched full-duplex operation.

A.text: Uses MAC addresses for forwarding decisions
A.rationale: Definition of Layer 2 switching.

B.text: Each port is a separate collision domain
B.rationale: A consequence of switched full-duplex.

C.rationale: That is a router (L3) function, unless it is a multilayer switch.

D.rationale: Role of a DHCP server.

E.rationale: TCP is Layer 4, outside the scope of a pure L2 switch.

161.question_text: Select TWO pieces of information a DHCP server provides to a client.
161.explanation: The typical DHCPOFFER/ACK message delivers at minimum the IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS server(s) and lease duration.

A.rationale: Core purpose of the lease.

B.rationale: DHCP option 3, required to leave the local network.

C.rationale: The MAC belongs to the client, not the server.

D.rationale: DHCP does not distribute routing tables.

162.explanation: OSPFv2 is a link-state IGP, an open standard (RFC 2328), that runs Dijkstra over the topology learned through LSAs. OSPFv3 is the equivalent for IPv6.

A.rationale: Each router advertises its links via LSAs.

B.rationale: Computes shortest path over the topological database.

C.rationale: That is RIP/EIGRP (hybrid), not OSPF.

D.rationale: That is EIGRP internal. OSPF has a default AD of 110.

E.text: Native IPv6 support with no additional config
E.rationale: OSPFv2 is IPv4-only. IPv6 requires OSPFv3.

163.explanation: A VLAN segments the broadcast domain and logically isolates user groups on the same physical infrastructure, without requiring re-cabling.

A.rationale: Each VLAN = one separate broadcast domain.

B.text: Logical traffic isolation between user groups
B.rationale: A user in one VLAN cannot reach another VLAN without routing.

C.rationale: No VLAN changes the physical cable capacity.

D.text: Removes the need for a router for inter-VLAN
D.rationale: On the contrary, one (or an SVI) is required to route between VLANs.

E.rationale: Role of DHCP, independent of VLANs.

164.explanation: STP port roles are: Root port (best path to root bridge), Designated port (chosen port on a segment), Alternate/Backup (RSTP). Trunk and Access are switching port modes, not STP roles.

A.rationale: Port with the lowest STP cost to the root bridge.

B.rationale: Port that forwards to a segment.

C.rationale: Port mode carrying multiple VLANs, not an STP role.

D.rationale: Port mode assigned to a single VLAN, not an STP role.

E.rationale: Informal term, not a standard STP role.

165.question_text: Select TWO true statements about PAT (NAT overload).
165.explanation: PAT lets many private addresses share ONE public address. The router keeps a translation table indexed on (inside IP, inside port) → (public IP, public port) to differentiate sessions.

A.text: Translates multiple private addresses to one public address
A.rationale: Definition of many-to-one.

B.text: Uses port numbers to differentiate simultaneous sessions
B.rationale: Ports become the demultiplexing key.

C.rationale: That is static NAT, not PAT.

D.text: Is not compatible with TCP connections
D.rationale: TCP is the main use case of PAT.

E.text: Requires a public address pool equal to the number of clients
E.rationale: PAT is precisely designed to save public addresses.

166.question_text: Select TWO rules regarding Cisco ACL application.
166.explanation: Key Cisco rules: only one ACL per direction per interface, an implicit "deny any" closes every ACL, extended ACL placed closest to the source, standard ACL closest to the destination.

A.text: Only one ACL per direction per interface
A.rationale: Two "in" ACLs on the same interface are not possible.

B.text: An implicit "deny any" is at the end of every ACL
B.rationale: Traffic not explicitly permitted is denied.

C.text: An extended ACL should be placed closest to the destination
C.rationale: Reverse: extended ACL closest to the source to filter early.

D.rationale: ACLs filter, they do not modify packets.

E.text: Numbered ACLs can be edited line-by-line like named ACLs
E.rationale: That is exactly the limitation of classic numbered ACLs.

167.question_text: Select TWO characteristics of the IaaS model.
167.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): the cloud provider manages the physical infrastructure and hypervisor; the customer manages the guest OS, applications and data. PaaS adds the runtime, SaaS delivers the finished application.

A.rationale: Core of IaaS.

B.text: The customer manages the guest OS and applications
B.rationale: Standard IaaS shared responsibility.

C.text: The provider manages the user applications
C.rationale: That is SaaS, not IaaS.

D.rationale: Object storage is one service among many.

E.text: Includes a managed development platform natively

168.question_text: Select TWO recommended modern Wi-Fi security protocols.
168.explanation: WPA2-Enterprise (802.1X + AES-CCMP) and WPA3 are the recommended modern protocols. WEP has been broken since 2001, original WPA (TKIP) is deprecated, Open provides no protection.

A.rationale: RADIUS authentication, AES-CCMP encryption.

B.rationale: SAE replaces the WPA2 handshake, offline-resistant.

C.rationale: RC4 vulnerabilities exploitable in minutes.

D.rationale: TKIP is deprecated by the Wi-Fi Alliance.

E.rationale: Cleartext traffic, interceptable by anyone in range.
